themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints surged to 15 reports THIS WEEK—a 253% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 4.2 weekly complaints—suggesting an acute pest control crisis in Greenwich Village/SoHo that demands immediate investigation into whether sanitation, construction, or seasonal factors are driving the spike.
evidence: 15 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for enhanced sanitation services and equipment
High volume of alteration permits (1525 filed in last 90 days) may indicate construction-related rodent displacement
reporting_angles: Interview residents in high-complaint blocks; map 311 complaints against active DOB construction permits to identify if renovations are displacing rodent colonies
Contact NYC Parks and HPD to understand whether this is part of a citywide trend or localized to CD102; investigate whether sanitation truck frequency is adequate

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees and Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 4 reports THIS WEEK (700% spike vs. 0.5 weekly average) and illegal tree damage spiked to 8 complaints LAST WEEK (392% increase vs. 1.6 weekly average)—signaling either environmental stress, contractor negligence, or inadequate city forestry maintenance in a historically tree-lined neighborhood.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.0, highest statistical severity)
8 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.43)
Forestry services and street tree maintenance is recurring CB budget priority, suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Walk affected blocks (identify via 311 data) and photograph tree conditions; interview residents about visible decline or contractor activity
Contact NYC Parks Forestry unit to determine if this reflects budget cuts, disease outbreak, or contractor violations; cross-reference with DOB permits for tree work

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaint Clustering
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 5 reports THIS WEEK—a 700% spike over the 0.6 weekly average—suggesting either rapid unlicensed dispensary proliferation, quality-of-life conflicts with neighbors, or enforcement action targeting operators in this district.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
Spike emerged suddenly without sustained prior trend, indicating new enforcement action or rapid business growth
High baseline vendor enforcement complaints (361 total over 90 days) suggest broader enforcement or quality-of-life tension in commercial corridors
reporting_angles: Identify locations of 311 complaints; visit areas to determine if unlicensed dispensaries are operating or if complaints reflect licensed storefront issues (odor, loitering, foot traffic)
Contact NYPD and State Cannabis Control Board to determine if enforcement actions are underway or if this reflects neighborhood opposition to new legal retailers

themes_detail.label: Drinking in Public Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints jumped to 3 reports THIS WEEK—a 500% spike from the 0.5 weekly baseline—potentially indicating a shift in police enforcement, post-pandemic behavioral changes, or concentrated street-drinking clusters that warrant on-the-ground verification.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0)
Encampment complaints remain high (487 over 90 days), suggesting possible intersection with homelessness or street conditions
Overlaps with recurring CB requests for public health and mental health programs
reporting_angles: Verify locations of 311 complaints on ground; determine if reports cluster on specific blocks or parks suggesting a hot spot
Interview NYPD precinct about enforcement strategy shift; contact mental health and social service providers about whether underlying homelessness or substance abuse is accelerating

themes_detail.label: Structural Defects in Buildings (Flooring/Stairs)
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stairs complaints spiked to 8 reports TWO WEEKS AGO—a 300% increase over the 2.0 weekly average—indicating concentrated building code violations that may reflect aging stock, deferred maintenance, or contractor negligence during the high volume of alterations (1525 filed in last 90 days).
evidence: 8 flooring/stairs complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 6.0)
1525 building alterations filed in past 90 days—highest permit category—suggests widespread renovation activity that may be generating code violations
HPD housing inspection expansion is recurring CB budget request, indicating systemic enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 flooring/stairs complaints against DOB alteration permits to identify buildings with both active work and safety violations; conduct building inspections
Interview HPD about inspection capacity and timelines; determine whether spike reflects new construction-related defects or discovery of deferred-maintenance issues in older buildings
